rationale: While speech delay is a common clinical feature in Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas neurodevelopmental syndrome (reported in ~78% to 93.3% across cohorts and literature compilations), published cohort characterizations directly contradict the hypothesis that speech delay occurs 'out of proportion to motor delay' in >85-90% of individuals. In the foundational cohort described in OMIM #620985 and cited by Zgheib et al., motor delay is documented at 88% (21 individuals) compared to speech delay at 78% (18 individuals). Karayol et al. specifically highlight prominent motor impairments including hypotonia, lack of coordination, and gait disturbance as core phenotypic hallmarks alongside global developmental delay.

evidence.text: In the OMIM clinical synopsis for Karayol-Borroto-Haghshenas syndrome (#620985), 21 patients exhibited motor delay, 18 had speech delay, 18 had hypotonia, and 11 had coordination abnormalities.
